toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Analyzer B most likely had a one-off QC outlier, not a real fault. The evidence: a single Level 2 potassium failure; a repeat from the same vial passed within 21 minutes; Levels 1 and 3 were normal. Level 2 averages are unchanged since the lot change (5.81 before, 5.80 after). Re-running 43 patient samples on Analyzer A gave differences of about +0.02 mmol/L, all within allowable limits. All QC ran on schedule (182 of 182), so the short-staffing theory isn't supported. I can't say whether a sampling glitch caused it, because the instrument doesn't flag partial aspirations on that line.

Ward 6's high potassiums look unrelated to the analyzers. Half the high results came from Analyzer A. Transport delays were longer for the high results (11 of 14 over 3 hours). The tube outage and four renal overflow patients are confounders, and no repeat samples have been requested.

What to sign off: return B to service and close the review with no amendments. Optionally add extra Level 2 QC for a week. Don't recall about 2,900 results, quarantine the lot, or widen the limits to ±4 SD. Ask Ward 6 for fresh samples from its high-potassium patients and get the tube station repaired. I haven't checked the instrument event log or vendor input, so my confidence is moderate.
